A01-D10 | Exhibition proposal

Document text extraction. layout and embedded images are not reproduced.

The end of written language? From cave paintings to emoji’s: Humans’ separation from nature Note In light of MindFuture’s recent reorganization and desire for proposals for one or more script-based projects with exhibition potential, this synopsis takes as its starting point a description of the exhibition moment itself. The description is the idea phase for a final conception and planning of the entire project’s course and adaption to the visibility of the new MindFuture. The Maze The exhibition area is shaped as a maze with a start and an end. The start is a terminal/console where the audience can enter a text or verbally ask a GAN-based AI/AM to design/present an image of the text. The image is generated using e.g. OpenAI (DALL-E) and presented on a big screen. The image is saved under a tag and then placed on a smaller screen consisting of a panel of mobile phones (e.g. iPhones, Samsung or other hardware providers) and will, as more images are generated, consist of hundreds of single images like a mosaic. In this mosaic the images can be placed according to different criteria (shape/figure, color, etc.) thereby creating a new big-screen image as a whole. This transition gets its own tag and is archived. Many images/tags can then be sorted into new motifs and provide the basis for writing a GPT-3 text based on the whole set of tags. The end result is thus a collaborative user-generated artwork that can be accessed e.g. via a website/app. Both images and texts can be saved as a file and/or printed on demand (e.g. as a pamphlet). The point Along the way an audience will experience state-of-the-art AI technologies and the application of algorithms as a new personal dialogue/use of the hardware they know from everyday life (smartphones,   pc/tv screens and photo apps etc.). They will also experience variations over personal assistants, chatbots etc., voice commands and translation to different languages and personal on-demand files/print etc. The experience The future interaction with technology for more than industry/workplace efficiency/optimizations and “ready-made” entertainment (TV series, films etc.) and to create one’s own art/literature. The purpose A de-dramatization of AI to think in creativity and innovation as ideas — i.e. more than just analysis and productivity to innovation as products and services. Visual art in a new automation phase. A new interpretation of symbolism in images. A growing skepticism that if algorithms can generate images (and text), what then are the future topics for artists, journalism and the media (including the role as reviewer/critic and “all kinds of taste judges”). Disruption? The exhibition is a kind of “hands on” and a personal engagement in culture, rather than just an observer of “technology and art” — i.e. if AI/AM can produce a personally experienced aha moment, what can AI/AM then become to everyday use of automation in the implications for politicians/business. Can we trust them? MindFuture’s role Is set in the world to provoke a debate on AI. The exhibition is an opportunity to involve hardware/software companies’ engagement e.g. via sponsorships, lending and demonstrations of gear and potential. It is conscious that this is not under the classic HW/SW exhibition pattern (incl. CES, IFA etc.), but the chance for companies to contribute PA/CSR moments (walk the talk, so to speak). The next phase is the conception and description of scope, participants, finances etc. Then the plan is executed. [████]
